title: Is Your Organization Scrappy?
author: Admired Leadership
summary: The post defines a scrappy organization as one that operates effectively with limited resources, substituting ingenuity and a hands-on, do-it-yourself approach for money and people. It describes the traits: action over perfection, speed over deliberation, risk-taking, and leaders who care more about the mission than their status. Most such cultures evolve from adversity, but the author argues the mindset can also be deliberately cultivated. Leaders foster it by modeling action, empowering rather than controlling, encouraging calculated experiments, and removing barriers to new ideas. A closing caution notes the scrappy chip on the shoulder is hard to knock off even after success.
points: Scrappiness is a resourcefulness-under-constraint culture that favors unconventional solutions over throwing people and money at problems.
Though usually born of adversity, the mindset can be manufactured by leaders on purpose.
Scrappy leaders put mission and team impact ahead of personal status, which attracts people who believe.
Fostering the culture means modeling action over perfection, valuing empowerment over control, and treating failure as learning.
quotes: Scrappy organizations make the most of what they have. It’s a hands-on and DIY (Do It Yourself) approach. The emphasis is on action over waiting for the perfect conditions or external validation.
Because they have a “scrappy mindset,” they prefer unconventional solutions and ideas. This gives leaders and team members a scrappy swagger derived from ingenuity and tenacity.

A history of facing adversity with scarce resources produces an uncommon grit. That doesn’t mean teams and organizations can’t become scrappy. While it’s most often a mindset born of necessity, it can be manufactured as well.

Scrappy organizations are resourceful and efficient. They value agility and speed over deliberation and circumspection. Risk-taking is considered essential for success, and leaders get highly involved with people and issues because they care deeply about quality.

As a rule, scrappy leaders care more about the mission and team impact than they do about their own status and position. This makes working inside a scrappy organization highly attractive to those who believe.

To foster a scrappy mindset, leaders model action over perfection and value empowerment over control. They insist that team members experiment and take calculated risks while treating failures as learning opportunities.
